findings.quote: Above a window head, a vertical joint is deliberately left free of mortar every half-metre or so.
findings.note: Genre/source-plausibility: authentic ELF single-question shorts open by orienting a lay reader in the first clause (host-2023-verb1-ELF-040 'The 16th- and 17th-century paintings of El Greco are populated by famously elongated figures'; var-2026-verb1-ELF-040 'People in 18th century Britain used the term criminal...'). This opens inside an unnamed cavity-wall assembly with no frame, and the piece then leans on unglossed building-trade vocabulary ('window head', 'outer skin', 'tray', 'stop end') that the exemplar shorts never require. It reads as a trade-journal excerpt rather than the general-interest magazine register ELF draws on.

findings.quote: The lull is when it lets go.
findings.note: Intellectual temperature/rhythm: the telegraphic, elliptical sentence rhythm sits outside the measured expository cadence of the short-text exemplars (host-2017-verb1-ELF-040 'Democracy and Education'), where clauses are long and fully specified. Not disqualifying on its own, but it compounds the register distance.
